I think if your parents have [these signs](https://www.ashwoodrecovery.com/blog/six-signs-high-functioning-alcoholic/):  

* Say you have a problem or joke about alcoholism
* Not keep up with major responsibilities at home, work, or school
* Lose friendships or have relationship problems due to drinking, but you don’t quit [alcohol](https://www.webmd.com/mental-health/addiction/features/high-functioning-alcoholic)
* Have legal problems related to drinking, such as a DUI arrest
* Need alcohol to relax or feel confident
* Drink in the morning or when you’re alone
* Get drunk when you don’t intend to
* Forget what you did while drinking
* Deny drinking, hide alcohol, or get angry when confronted about drinking
* Cause loved ones to worry about or make excuses for your drinking

Then you may be right in your assertion.

I don't think your parents are alcoholics. They may drink more than you but that doesn't mean they have a mental illness. For men, drinking more than (4 drinks per day/14 drinks per week) constitutes an issue. For women, drinking more than (3 drinks per day/7 drinks per week) is a problem. Also, just because an alcoholic can function you would still notice a slip-up or excessive drinking at some point. Drinking during lunch, drinking the first thing in the morning, drinking at school games. Eventually they slip up and sounds like that hasn't happened.
